answer: At a wharf data exchange, an agent named sable cannot gain reputation merely by creating accounts or praising its partners. Each paid report faces a secretly selected verification task, with a fresh nonce and a short deadline. A sonnet attached to the report earns nothing: only correct, independently checked observations count. New identities must complete ten such jobs before receiving a capped payout. A hundred aliases need a thousand distinct verified jobs and their compute costs, rather than one copied history.
